extracted.intended_audience: freelance editors, the writers and publishers who hire them, editorial specialists, and prospective course instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program rules for delivering and taking online editorial professional-development offerings (webinars, traditional courses, intensives, and self-paced courses) run by the Editorial Freelancers Association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance registration required
rubrics_metrics.description: Most courses are open to members and nonmembers; all require advance registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed information about registration, accessibility, duration of access, and refund policies is on the class registration and information page. Enrollment is limited for many offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member benefits and pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Members enjoy 20% off the regular fee for all courses, and get access to some webinars for free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership discounts apply at registration; webinars and some course recordings may be free to members. Recorded webinars are also available for purchase to nonmembers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Webinar format and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: EFA webinars are a low-cost, quick way to improve editorial skills, learn to boost your business, and hear from industry experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some webinars are introductory overviews; others are deep dives into technical subjects (e.g., copyediting data tables). All webinars are recorded; real-time webinars take place on Zoom and are auto-captioned; recordings are professionally captioned and hosted on the education site. Everyone who registers for a live webinar will receive access to the recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional course structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional courses are asynchronous on a set schedule: content is released one week at a time over four to six weeks, with weekly assignments and instructor feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students complete weekly assignments, receive instructor feedback, discuss topics in an online forum, and attend one or two live Q&A sessions. Access to materials lasts 90 days after the course ends. Enrollment is limited and most traditional courses run at least once or twice a year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional course learning goals and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional courses are intended for professional development; there is no grading or pass/fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon finishing a course, you will receive a certificate of completion. Emphasis is on detailed feedback, peer support, and time to explore complex topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensive format and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensives are live classes held over two consecutive weekdays with three to four hours of instruction per day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They combine lectures, group conversation, activities, and real-time feedback. Sessions take place on Zoom and are auto-captioned. Recordings are provided to participating students only. These classes are usually live-only and don’t usually repeat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensive class size and interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensives have limited enrollment to allow hands-on instruction and personal interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small class sizes ensure plenty of opportunity for real-time guidance, practice, and getting to know classmates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-paced course characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-paced courses give access to all content at once so learners can move through lessons at their own pace; many function as references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They provide in-depth lessons, self-assessments in video and text, and regular Q&A sessions with the instructor via Zoom. Access to self-paced courses lasts one year. Materials may be downloaded for personal use only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access duration by course type
rubrics_metrics.description: Course materials access period varies by format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional courses: access to materials lasts 90 days after the course ends. Self-paced courses: one-year access. Webinar recordings: registrants receive access; recorded webinars are available for purchase. Intensive recordings: provided to participating students only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captioning and accessibility of live and recorded content
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time webinars and sessions are auto-captioned; recorded webinars and recordings are professionally captioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings are hosted on the education site. The page also points to a class registration and information page for additional accessibility details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of completion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants receive a certificate of completion upon finishing a course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses are professional-development oriented with no formal grading or pass/fail; certificates document completion rather than assessed competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor recruitment scope
rubrics_metrics.description: EFA seeks instructors for courses in all levels of editing across fiction, nonfiction, and specialties (technical, academic, scientific, medical, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audiences include freelance editors, the writers who hire them, staff editors, publishing professionals, and other editorial professionals. Members of marginalized communities are especially encouraged to submit pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor proposal and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective instructors must read instructor information and submit a proposal for the desired course type (webinar, intensive, traditional, self-paced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the appropriate button for the type of course you want to propose. The EFA welcomes niche ideas and diverse perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor compensation and support
rubrics_metrics.description: EFA offers long lead times for course creation, fair, equitable standardized fees, and support with syllabus development and using the course site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA handles all aspects of administration, including processing enrollments and registrations, and promotes courses in newsletters and social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Downloaded course materials are for personal use only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students may download materials they want to keep for further study, but the usage is restricted to personal study (not redistribution or commercial use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and cost trade-offs by format
rubrics_metrics.description: Different formats offer trade-offs in time commitment, interactivity, and cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intensives: minimal calendar time (two consecutive weekdays), lower price than a traditional course, live engagement. Traditional courses: more time to explore topics, detailed feedback, higher time commitment over weeks. Self-paced: low cost, immediate access, no waitlists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundled learning pathways and cataloging
rubrics_metrics.description: EFA bundles selected webinars and courses to help learners who are just getting started or branching into new areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A course catalog groups recommended starting points. This helps reduce overwhelm and makes it easier to find appropriate offerings.
